research_questions.statement: How can single-cell perturbation responses be learned from unpaired control and perturbed cell populations?

provenance.text_excerpt: we illustrate that CellOT generalizes well on unseen settings by (1) predicting the scRNA-seq responses of holdout patients with lupus exposed to interferon-β and patients with glioblastoma to panobinostat; (2) inferring lipopolysaccharide responses across different species; and (3) modeling the hematopoietic developmental trajectories of different subpopulations.

claims.statement: CellOT generalizes well to unseen patients and species.

provenance.text_excerpt: While the autoencoder baselines tend to capture the mean of the treated cell population, they are less successful in matching all heterogeneous states of the perturbed population (higher moments of the perturbed population). ... claims.statement: CellOT captures higher moments of perturbed distributions, unlike autoencoder baselines.

experiments_or_tasks: Benchmarked against scGEN, cAE, and PopAlign on proteomic (4i) and scRNA-seq datasets.
CellOT learns an optimal transport map for each perturbation by parameterizing dual potentials with input convex neural networks.

methods.name: CellOT
methods.protocol_description: Learns optimal transport map Tk = ∇gk, where gk is a convex neural network parameterizing the dual potential. Applied on latent representations from an autoencoder for scRNA-seq data.
